newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rebels take new southern town.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebels take new southern town.

text.p: Another major town in southern Albania, Berat, has come under rebel control after the army withdrew en masse, a spokesman for rebel forces said on Monday.

The spokesman said the army moved out of its barracks on Sunday after a television broadcast showed President Sali Berisha and opposition parties signing an agreement on a national unity government and new elections.

A doctor at the hospital in Berat, one of Albania's most ancient towns, said one person had been killed and 20 slightly injured in random shooting, but there had been no clashes between rebels and security forces. Shots rang out throughout the town and most residents remained indoors to avoid stray bullets.

The rebel spokesman said insurgents supported the idea of a caretaker government as proposed during Sunday's agreement in Tirana. But they insisted on the resignation of Berisha, whom they blamed for allowing pyramid schemes to flourish before collapsing with the savings of hundreds of thousands of people.
"We don't trust him any more," said Sokol, one of the rebels. "He deserves to be hanged by his tongue."

Rebels have now extended their control over most of Albania's southern districts. Berisha was meeting leaders of political parties in Tirana to determine the make-up of the interim government pending elections in June.
